title: Add SLO tier labels + error budget helpers for tiered batching rollouts
author: Aisha Bello
release_notes: SLO toolkit now supports a first-class `slo_tier` label (fast/standard/cost_efficient) and provides helpers to compute and compare error budget burn by tier across latency SLOs.
description:
Context: As part of tiered workload-aware batching defaults, SRE needs to compare latency/error budgets across the three SLO tiers (fast/standard/cost_efficient) during staged rollouts and while responding to incidents. Today, the slo-toolkit only understands service/env/route labels and the dashboards are forced to infer tiers from ad-hoc route naming. This PR adds a standardized `slo_tier` label and a small set of helpers to produce tier-aware burn-rate queries + summaries.

What’s in this PR: (1) Adds canonical tier label support to slo-toolkit’s label normalization: `slo_tier` ∈ {fast, standard, cost_efficient}; includes parser/validator + a mapping helper for legacy values (`eco`, `cost-efficient`, `cost_efficient`) to the canonical form. (2) Adds error budget tracking helpers that aggregate burn by tier for latency SLOs (p95/p99), including a “compare tiers” helper that returns aligned time series suitable for dashboards. (3) Updates example queries and README snippets to show how to instrument and query burn by tier, plus adds a migration note for teams that currently encode tier in route names.

Why here (and not in the runtime repo): the SLO definitions + burn-rate query generation live in slo-toolkit and are reused by our internal dashboard generator + alert config templates; this keeps tier semantics consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.

Testing: unit tests for label normalization + query output shape; golden tests for PromQL templates; CI runs `go test ./...` and lint.

Rollout: backwards compatible. If `slo_tier` is not present, helpers treat it as `standard` (configurable default) and emit a warning metric `slo_toolkit_label_missing_total{label="slo_tier"}` to help drive adoption.

Follow-ups: once this lands, ENG-18427 will wire tiered dashboards/alerts to the new label and remove the remaining route-name inference logic.
commits: 1) slo: add slo_tier label constants + normalization rules 2) slo: promql templates for tiered burn + compare helper 3) tests: golden coverage for tier queries 4) docs: add tiered SLO usage examples + migration notes
files_changed: pkg/labels/normalize.go (add slo_tier canonicalization + legacy mapping); pkg/labels/normalize_test.go (table tests for tier parsing); pkg/promql/templates.go (tier label injection + burn-rate templates); pkg/budget/burn.go (tier-aware aggregation helpers); pkg/budget/burn_test.go (golden output for tier compare); pkg/warnings/metrics.go (missing-label counter); examples/promql/tiered-latency-burn.promql (new example); docs/tiered-slos.md (new doc); docs/migration/2025-03-slo-tier-label.md (migration note); .golangci.yml (enable exhaustive for tier enum); README.md (updated snippets)
conversation:
Sean Gallagher (review): The canonical values look right. Can we avoid defaulting missing `slo_tier` to standard? That could hide instrumentation gaps during rollout. Also, please confirm label name aligns with the rest of the SLO stack (`slo_tier` vs `tier`).

Aisha Bello (author): Agree on visibility. I kept the default for backwards compatibility in existing dashboards, but added `slo_toolkit_label_missing_total{label="slo_tier"}` and a log warning. Happy to also add an option to make missing tier “unknown” so alert owners can choose strictness.

Rafael Mendes (review): +1 on making strict mode possible. Also: cost_efficient naming—runtime uses `cost_efficient` in config, but product copy sometimes says “cost-efficient”. Your legacy mapping covers it, good. Please add a note about streaming routes: some endpoints will run fast tier but still be more sensitive to queue delay; we’ll want to segment by route + tier.

Aisha Bello (author): Added `NormalizeSLOTier(..., StrictMissing bool)` and documented recommended usage: dashboards can remain permissive; alerts for rollout can be strict. Updated docs to emphasize route segmentation still applies.

Sergio Costa (review): The compare helper currently returns p95 and p99 series in a fixed order; can we make it explicit in the function name or return shape? This bit us before in grafana dashboards.

Aisha Bello (author): Renamed to `CompareLatencyBurnByTier(p95, p99)` and updated the docs snippet to show explicit construction. Also added golden tests verifying labelset ordering.

Logan Wright (review): Minor: metric name `slo_toolkit_label_missing_total` should include `component="labels"` label for our internal conventions. Not blocking.

Aisha Bello (author): Added `component` label and updated test expectations.

Sean Gallagher (final): Looks good with strict mode and warning metric. Approved.

Rafael Mendes (final): Approved. This unblocks tiered rollout monitoring.

Merge: Squash merge after green CI.
